title: Compact bucketization and prefix-aware batcher to reduce padding and KV cache fragmentation
author: Maya Chen
description: Motivation: current seqlen bucketing uses fixed-width buckets which leaves significant per-batch padding for workloads with bimodal and prefix-heavy distributions. This also increases KV cache fragmentation when many requests share short prefixes followed by diverse suffix lengths. This PR introduces a compact bucketization strategy combined with a prefix-aware batching heuristic to both minimize padding and maximize KV cache reuse. Approach summary: 1) Compact bucketization: instead of fixed buckets we quantize sequence lengths using an exponential binning (ceil(log2(len))) combined with a local density split to avoid overly wide upper bins. This keeps buckets tight where request density is high and allows coarse grouping for long tails. 2) Prefix-aware batching: requests that share a prefix length (or exact prefix hash) are preferentially co-batched so they can reuse the same KV cache slices and avoid repeated prefix decode work. A lightweight fingerprint is computed from the first N tokens (configurable, default 8) and used as a soft affinity key. 3) Kernel hinting: we propagate bucket metadata to the kernel selector so that kernels optimized for similar sequence-length patterns (e.g., rnn-friendly padding vs attention-optimized kernels) are preferred. 4) Rollout: feature gate runtime.flag.compact_prefix_batcher with gradual rollout by traffic percentage and an endpoint-level override. Implementation notes: - Changes in src/runtime/batcher.cpp: new CompactBucketizer class, affinity slot accounting, updated continuous-batching loop to build micro-batches using prefix affinity and cardinality limits. - Changes in src/runtime/kernels/selector.cpp: accept bucket_hint and affinity_hint and select kernel paths accordingly. - KV cache: improved coalescing when prefix_affinity present; added eviction policy tweak to prefer contiguous prefix slices. - Config and operators: added flags in config/runtime.yaml and CLI --compact-prefix-batcher-enabled. - Tests: unit tests for boundary bucket edges and affinity collisions in tests/unit/test_bucketizer.cpp; perf harness in tests/perf/bench_prefix_reuse.py and integration smoke in tests/e2e/batching_affinity.smoke. Perf results (internal perf lab, nv4-like GPUs, mixed chat workload with short prefixes): - 95th-percentile latency: -9% (from 210ms to 191ms) - P50 latency: -6% - Tokens/sec per-GPU: +14% effective throughput due to less padding - Cost-per-request estimate: -12% at target load - KV cache hit-rate for prefix reuse scenarios: +22% Observability: added metrics runtime.batch.bucket_size, runtime.batch.affinity_hit, runtime.kv.prefix_reuse_rate and dashboards in observability-pack under dashboards/batching-prefix-affinity.json Compatibility and safety: - No API changes. Behavior is feature-gated and disabled by default. - Added comprehensive unit and perf tests. - Microbenchmarked kernel selection overhead; overhead <0.4% at high QPS. Rollout plan: enable 1% traffic for 24h -> 10% 48h -> 50% 72h -> 100% pending metrics. Checklist: - [x] Compact bucketizer implementation - [x] Prefix affinity hash and co-batching - [x] Kernel hint plumbing - [x] Unit & perf tests - [x] Observability and dashboards - [x] Feature flag + rollout plan Related: builds on ENG-5230 (seqlen bucketing primitives) and complements ENG-5761 (kv cache consolidation).

review_comments: Ethan Park: Nice approach, can you clarify how affinity interacts with autoscaling micro-batching? In particular, will affinity cause head-of-line blocking when waiting for matching prefixes?

Maya Chen: We use a soft-affinity (best-effort) with a per-batch time-budget. The batcher will not wait beyond the micro-batch timeout; affinity only reorders candidates and does not stall the fill loop. Added comments and a diagram in batcher.cpp explaining the path.

Lena Gómez: Add unit tests for the bucket boundary at powers of two and around the local density split points. Also please document the config knobs with recommended defaults for typical chat workloads.
Maya Chen: Added the requested unit tests and expanded config docs with recommended defaults. Noted expected behavior for corner cases (len==0, len==max_seq).
Rajiv Menon: Kernel selector change looks good; can you make the hint optional to avoid touching legacy kernels? Also check that the hint propagation doesn't copy heavy structs per-request.
Maya Chen: Kernel hint is optional; selector falls back to existing logic if bucket_hint is empty. Hints are passed as small enums/ints to avoid per-request heavy copies.
release_notes: Introduce a feature-gated compact bucketizer and prefix-aware batching heuristic to reduce padding and improve KV cache reuse. Expected improvements for prefix-heavy chat workloads: lower p95 latency and up to ~12% cost reduction. Disabled by default; enable via runtime.flag.compact_prefix_batcher.
perf_summary: Mixed chat workload: p95 -9%, p50 -6%, tokens/sec +14%, kv prefix hit +22%
notes: This PR intentionally keeps the affinity key size small (N=8 tokens by default). If customers find affinity over-aggressive, the flag allows lowering N or disabling affinity while keeping compact bucketization enabled.
